name: Veldtmann Pressline Assembly Full Kit
description: A factory floor assembly kit designed for the pressline environment — heat, machine noise, and twelve-hour standing shifts. The core garment is a fitted navy coverall in heavy synth-denim with a Veldtmann WorkCo embroidered patch on the right chest and a name patch on the left, along with hi-vis orange contrast stitching at every seam and pocket edge. The coverall has a back zip running from collar to mid-spine with a secondary flap that conceals and protects a spinal rig channel — a standard feature on Veldtmann's aug-accommodating line. Sleeves can be rolled and secured with internal button tabs for lathe-adjacent work. Over the coverall, a short charcoal utility apron with two wide front pockets and a magnetic tool strip at the waist provides additional protection for the torso. The gloves are heat-resistant synth-leather in dark grey with reinforced palm panels, tucked into the left apron pocket when not in use. Footwear is a pair of broad-last steel-toe work shoes in matte black with anti-static outsoles and a quick-lace retention system. A navy hard-shell bump cap with a Veldtmann logo sits on the crown, its inner foam compressed by years of use.
materials: hard-shell ABS bump cap with foam liner
functionality: Spinal rig channel with protective back flap, rollable sleeves with internal button tabs, anti-static footwear for electronics-adjacent environments, magnetic tool strip for fast-access hardware, heat-resistant glove integration, corponation ID patching system for access zone verification.
what_it_says: You know every sound your machine makes and what each deviation means. The bump cap is dented on the left side from an incident three years ago that you don't talk about. You take pride in a clean coverall at the start of a shift even if it's ruined by hour four. Reliable. Experienced. Not management and fine with that.
worn_by: production shift leads who still work the line
manufacturer: Veldtmann WorkCo (corponation-issued, standard factory floor uniform program)
story_hooks: A Veldtmann pressline worker slips the players a data chip wrapped in a heat-resistant glove — it contains shift production logs showing the factory has been running a third shift that doesn't appear in any official schedule.
The magnetic tool strip on a specific worker's apron holds something that isn't a tool — a small, very dense object that someone will pay a great deal to recover or destroy.
The bump cap's interior foam has been hollowed out and used as a concealment space for years; the worker who wore it has just been transferred, and they left something inside.

physical_description.visual_profile: A utilitarian factory uniform that reads as purposeful and durable. The navy coverall forms a structured silhouette, broken only by high-visibility orange thread that traces every seam and pocket, creating a grid-like visual emphasis. The charcoal apron layers over the torso, anchoring the outfit to the work environment. Steel-toe shoes ground the wearer in industrial practicality. The bump cap completes the image of a Tier 3 assembly-line worker—functional, regulated, augmentation-ready.
physical_description.fit: Fitted through the shoulders and torso with enough room for movement and layering. The coverall accommodates a straight leg without excess fabric. The apron drapes loose enough to allow bending and reaching but stays secured at the waist. Sleeves are purposefully cut to roll and tab-lock.
physical_description.primary_material: Heavy synth-denim coverall; charcoal canvas apron; synth-leather gloves; reinforced synthetic rubber shoe outsoles
physical_description.texture: Crisp, structured denim with a slight sheen from industrial treatment. Orange contrast stitching creates tactile ridges. Apron canvas is matte and slightly stiff. Gloves are smooth yet slightly tacky for grip. Shoes have a scuffed, broken-in matte finish.
physical_description.color_scheme: Core navy coverall with charcoal apron overlay. Hi-vis orange stitching throughout. Matte black steel-toe shoes. Dark grey heat-resistant gloves. Navy bump cap with embroidered logo.
physical_description.closures: Primary back zip on coverall (collar to mid-spine, concealing spinal rig channel). Magnetic tool strip on apron waist. Button tabs on coverall sleeves for roll-lock. Quick-lace shoe retention system. Apron pockets sit open.
distinctive_features: Concealed spinal rig channel with protective flap on back zip
Embroidered Veldtmann WorkCo patch on right chest
Name patch on left chest (personalization point)
Hi-vis orange contrast stitching at every seam and pocket edge (safety compliance)
Rollable sleeves with internal button tabs
Worn/compressed foam inner bumpcap (evidence of repeated use)
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3 — working class, corpo-issued standard uniform. Not luxury, but reliable and regulated.
physical_description.cultural_context: Wears this garment signals factory floor labor, specifically pressline assembly work. Suggests augmentation compatibility (spinal rig channel). Marks wearer as Veldtmann WorkCo employee—regulated, tracked, part of a large industrial organism.
physical_description.condition_typical: Broken-in but maintained. The bump cap shows years of compression. Stitching is clean and intact. Possible grease stains on apron from shift work, but generally presentable—company issue requires standard appearance.
